PullRequest.Title: agentHost: restore browser tunnel payload compatibility
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

Restore browser tunnel receive limits to the **100 MiB** message allowance used by the former vscode.dev server-side proxy and the desktop tunnel client (`ws`'s default `maxPayload`).

- Apply the same finite 100 MiB ceiling to frames and assembled messages, since a complete response can arrive in one frame.
- Preserve the close code and log the underlying relay error instead of only an empty close reason.
- Cover 12 MiB unfragmented and fragmented responses, rejection above 100 MiB, custom lower limits, and normal/error close logging.

No pagination, UI changes, desktop framing changes, or gateway changes.

## Why

Moving tunnel handling from the server-side web proxy into the browser introduced a 1 MiB frame limit and an 8 MiB message limit. The host could still send a larger saved conversation, causing the browser to disconnect with `Transport lost (reconnecting)`.

Aligning the frame limit with 8 MiB was insufficient: a subsequent local reproduction logged an incoming 11,212,921-byte frame (about 10.7 MiB), which exceeded that message ceiling. This update restores the previous receive-size allowance rather than selecting another intermediate cap.

The former proxy also forwarded complete messages to the browser for parsing and rendering. This is a compatibility fix, not a claim that rendering a 100 MiB history is responsive. Browser-side framing adds work compared with the old path; broader history-loading performance work is outside this PR.

## Validation

- Confirmed four updated regression cases fail under the 8 MiB ceiling.
- Targeted WebSocket-over-duplex and tunnel connector unit suites: **34 passing** with the restored ceiling.
- ESLint: passed for all four PR files.
- Staged-file hygiene: passed, including normal commit hooks.
- Targeted source transpilation completed. No full application build or end-to-end UI run.

Scenarios.Scenario: Browser tunnel reconnect receives and restores a large saved conversation in one WebSocket message
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The tunnel stream must receive the full frame/message, WebSocketFrameParser must assemble a contiguous payload, TextDecoder must create the string, and BrowserTunnelConnectionTransport synchronously JSON.parse it before the protocol consumer can process the restored conversation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open a WebSocket over an existing Dev Tunnels relay stream and receive the agent-host protocol response.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One upgraded relay stream per active connection and one inbound network message per logical protocol response; stream chunking or WebSocket fragmentation does not create additional network requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same relay/WebSocket boundary existed, but the browser framing layer rejected frames above 1 MiB and assembled messages above 8 MiB; this diff accepts up to 100 MiB.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The full response must arrive before decoding, JSON parsing, and restoration can proceed.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Incoming saved-conversation payload size, now bounded at 100 MiB. Parser buffering, contiguous assembly, UTF-8 decoding, and downstream JSON parsing grow linearly with message bytes; effective cardinality is one complete protocol message after fragmentation is coalesced.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Frame processing is synchronous and serialized per stream data event. A normal connection handles one message at a time; separate active tunnel connections can process independently, with no new concurrency burst introduced by the diff.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is involved in frame/message receipt or parsing; cold and warm behavior are equivalent, with no coalescing beyond assembling fragments into one message.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that larger accepted messages cause proportionally larger buffering, decoding, and synchronous JSON parsing. However, this is the bounded work required to restore the previously supported message range, not evidence of avoidable repeated work or an introduced boundary.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: An approximately 11 MiB frame is evidenced by the change and covered at 12 MiB in tests, but prevalence of messages approaching the 100 MiB ceiling and browser-specific pause duration are not measured.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The diff deliberately restores compatibility for large responses with a finite cap matching the existing Node transport. It does not add network calls, fan-out, concurrency, or unbounded retention, and the review found no narrower existing transport API or surgical correction that preserves the required large-message behavior while proving a concrete regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Browser tunnel gateway selection and normal agent-host protocol traffic
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Management lookup, relay connection, forwarded-port connection, WebSocket upgrade, and the gateway selection acknowledgement must complete before an active agent-host connection is returned.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch tunnel metadata from the Dev Tunnels management service.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One management request per connection or selection attempt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical management request count and placement.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before creating and connecting the relay client.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Connect the Dev Tunnels relay client.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One relay connection per connection or selection attempt, with a bounded retry only on gateway-selection rejection in unchanged code.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before the forwarded port and WebSocket are usable.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Write one HTTP upgrade request and await one WebSocket upgrade response over the relay stream.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One upgrade exchange per opened message socket.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical upgrade exchange; only post-upgrade payload limits were lower.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before gateway or active protocol messages can flow.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Gateway inventory and acknowledgement messages are small single logical messages; tunnel count does not multiply operations inside the changed hunks.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Connection steps are awaited in sequence. The diff changes no limiter, queue, retry, or parallelism behavior.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Tunnel metadata loading follows existing SDK/service behavior; the changed payload constants do not alter cache keys, warm-cache behavior, coalescing, or negative caching.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the unchanged caller and connector flow that boundary cardinality and critical-path ordering are unchanged.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact management and relay latency depends on the network, but the diff introduces no additional boundary operation or waiting point.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. Raising receive limits does not affect ordinary small gateway/protocol messages and adds no repeated work, fan-out, or critical-path boundary.

Scenarios.Scenario: Relay socket closes normally or fails due to a protocol/payload error
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Closure happens after the connection can no longer make progress. The connector emits one log entry, disposes the TunnelConnection, socket, and relay client, then notifies consumers of closure.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Emit one info log for a normal close or one warning containing the underlying error for a failed close.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one log call per socket-close event because TunnelMessageSocket finishClose fires once.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same close path emitted one info log; the diff changes severity and adds the error message without increasing call count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The log occurs synchronously on the terminal close path but does not delay an otherwise-progressing connection.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of socket closures; message size affects at most the temporary buffers held by that closing socket, not log count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One close callback per connection. Different connections may close independently; the diff introduces no burst scheduling.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that TunnelConnection.dispose removes listeners, closes/disposes the socket, disposes the relay client, and releases the connection from the map, so the raised limit does not create persistent post-close retention.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Log sink implementation cost varies, but call cardinality remains one and the added string is bounded by the Error message.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. Error logging replaces rather than adds a boundary call, and close ownership releases large fragmented buffers for garbage collection.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all four changed files and traced the browser receive, gateway startup, synchronous decode/JSON parse, logging, and cleanup paths. The payload-cap increase permits larger linear buffering and parsing by design, but remains finite, restores an established transport allowance, and introduces no extra boundary calls, multiplicative work, concurrency burst, cache defect, or retained-resource lifecycle bug. No high-confidence actionable performance finding was identified.
